facts.name: Defined Declared Combat Zone
facts.sentence: A 'declared combat zone' is defined within the policy.

facts.name: Declared Combat Zone Definition
facts.sentence: A 'Declared Combat Zone' is any area designated as a combat zone by Executive Order of the President of the United States.

facts.name: Declared Combat Zone Definition
facts.sentence: A 'Declared Combat Zone' is any area designated as a combat zone by declaration of the Secretary of Defense.

facts.name: Friendly Fire Definition
facts.sentence: A 'Friendly Fire' incident refers to death caused by the armed forces of the United States or its allies.

facts.name: Friendly Fire Definition Clarification
facts.sentence: A 'Friendly Fire' incident excludes deaths resulting from enemy action.

facts.name: Line of Duty Definition
facts.sentence: The term 'Line of Duty' describes any act or occurrence arising from the performance of official military duties.

facts.name: Line of Duty Requirement
facts.sentence: An act or occurrence qualifies as 'Line of Duty' only when it is ordered or directed by a superior officer.

facts.name: Line of Duty Definition
facts.sentence: An act or occurrence qualifies as 'Line of Duty' only when it is governed by military regulation.

facts.name: Occupational Separation Definition
facts.sentence: An 'Occupational Separation' includes honorable discharge from active duty service.

facts.name: Retirement Included
facts.sentence: An 'Occupational Separation' includes retirement from active duty service.

facts.name: Occupational Separation Definition
facts.sentence: An 'Occupational Separation' includes release from active duty service.

facts.name: Full Combat Coverage
facts.sentence: This policy provides full death benefit coverage for death occurring in any combat zone.

facts.name: Enemy Action Coverage
facts.sentence: Death from enemy action is covered under this policy’s full combat coverage.

facts.name: Hostile Fire Coverage
facts.sentence: Death from hostile fire is covered under this policy’s full combat coverage.

facts.name: IED Deaths Covered
facts.sentence: Death from improvised explosive devices (IEDs) is covered under this policy’s full combat coverage.

facts.name: Friendly Fire Coverage
facts.sentence: Death from friendly fire while on deployment is covered under this policy’s full combat coverage.

facts.name: Training Accident Coverage
facts.sentence: Death from training accidents at any domestic installation is covered under this policy’s full combat coverage.

facts.name: Training Accident Coverage
facts.sentence: Death from training accidents at any overseas installation is covered under this policy’s full combat coverage.

facts.name: Disease Coverage During Deployment
facts.sentence: Death from disease or illness contracted while on deployment is covered under this policy’s full combat coverage.

facts.name: R&R Coverage Inclusion
facts.sentence: Death occurring during authorized rest and recuperation (R&R) is covered under this policy’s full combat coverage.

facts.name: Waiver of War Exclusions
facts.sentence: This policy constitutes an express waiver of all standard war exclusions.

facts.name: Waiver Scope Specificity
facts.sentence: The waiver of standard war exclusions applies specifically to this policy.

facts.name: Waiver of War Exclusions
facts.sentence: The waiver of standard war exclusions is granted in consideration of military surcharges collected.

facts.name: Unauthorized Absence Exclusion
facts.sentence: Death occurring while the insured is in Unauthorized Absence (UA) is excluded from coverage.

facts.name: AWOL Exclusion Clause
facts.sentence: Death occurring while the insured is in AWOL status is excluded from coverage.

facts.name: UA/AWOL Exclusion Exception
facts.sentence: If death occurs while the insured is in UA or AWOL status, the exclusion applies unless certain conditions are met.

facts.name: Prisoner of War Exception
facts.sentence: If death occurs while the insured is in UA or AWOL status and the insured is later found to have been a prisoner of war, the exclusion does not apply.

facts.name: Duress Exception to UA/AWOL Exclusion
facts.sentence: If death occurs while the insured is in UA or AWOL status and the insured is later found to have been under duress, the exclusion does not apply.

facts.name: Voluntary Collaboration Exclusion
facts.sentence: No death benefit is payable if death results directly from the insured's voluntary collaboration with a foreign adversary.

facts.name: Treason Exclusion
facts.sentence: No death benefit is payable if death results directly from the insured committing treason against the United States.

facts.name: Treason Collaboration Exclusion
facts.sentence: No benefit is payable if death occurs as a direct consequence of the insured's voluntary collaboration with a foreign adversary.

facts.name: Treason Exclusion Clause
facts.sentence: No benefit is payable if death occurs as a direct consequence of the insured's commission of treason against the United States.

facts.name: Treason Exclusion Standard
facts.sentence: Treason against the United States must be established by a final court-martial finding to trigger the exclusion.

facts.name: Treason Exclusion Standard
facts.sentence: Treason against the United States must be established by a federal court judgment to trigger the exclusion.

facts.name: Suicide Exclusion Clause
facts.sentence: Death by suicide within 2 years of the policy date limits the benefit to a return of premiums paid.

facts.name: Honorably Separated Surcharge Return
facts.sentence: If the insured separates honorably from active duty, the military occupation surcharge is returned.

facts.name: Surcharge Credit on Separation
facts.sentence: The military occupation surcharge is returned as a credit to future premiums.

facts.name: Pro-Rated Surcharge Credit
facts.sentence: The credit for the military occupation surcharge is pro-rated for months remaining in that policy year.

facts.name: Civilian Transition Continuity
facts.sentence: Coverage continues uninterrupted when the insured separates honorably from active duty.

facts.name: Traumatic Injury Rider
facts.sentence: Rider 1 is titled 'Traumatic Injury / Combat Wounds Rider'.

facts.name: Annual Premium for Rider 1
facts.sentence: The annual premium for Rider 1 is $135.

facts.name: Traumatic Injury Benefit
facts.sentence: Rider 1 pays a lump-sum benefit if the insured sustains a qualifying traumatic injury in the line of duty.

facts.name: Permanent Impairment Requirement
facts.sentence: A qualifying traumatic injury must result in permanent impairment to trigger payment under Rider 1.

facts.name: Rider Benefit Trigger
facts.sentence: Rider 1 pays upon injury, not death.

facts.name: Rider 1 Payment Does Not Reduce Death Benefit
facts.sentence: Payment under Rider 1 does not reduce the death benefit.

facts.name: Trauma Benefit: Bilateral Limb Loss
facts.sentence: Loss of both hands or feet, or one of each, qualifies for a $200,000 benefit.

facts.name: Loss of Both Eyes Benefit
facts.sentence: Loss of sight in both eyes qualifies for a $200,000 benefit.

facts.name: Combined Limb and Eye Injury Benefit
facts.sentence: Loss of one hand or foot AND loss of one eye qualifies for a $150,000 benefit.

facts.name: One Hand or Foot Loss Benefit
facts.sentence: Loss of one hand or foot alone qualifies for a $100,000 benefit.

facts.name: Eye Injury Benefit
facts.sentence: Loss of sight in one eye qualifies for a $75,000 benefit.

facts.name: TBIs Qualify for $100K Payout
facts.sentence: Traumatic brain injury rated moderate to severe by the VA qualifies for a $100,000 benefit.

facts.name: Burns Qualification Benefit
facts.sentence: 50% or more burns to the face, body, or both qualify for a $150,000 benefit.

facts.name: One-Time Injury Payment
facts.sentence: Each injury benefit under Rider 1 is payable only once.

facts.name: Lifetime Benefit Cap
facts.sentence: The total lifetime benefit cap for Rider 1 is $200,000.

facts.name: Rider Continuation Post-Payment
facts.sentence: Rider 1 remains in force after a traumatic injury benefit is paid.

facts.name: Death Benefit Unaffected
facts.sentence: The death benefit is unaffected by the payment of a traumatic injury benefit.

facts.name: Trauma Injury Payout Limit
facts.sentence: The trauma injury benefit is payable once.

facts.name: Lifetime Rider Benefit Cap
facts.sentence: The total rider benefit is capped at $200,000 lifetime.

facts.name: Rider Continuation Post-Payout
facts.sentence: The rider continues in force after the traumatic injury benefit is paid.

facts.name: Death Benefit Unaffected
facts.sentence: The death benefit is unaffected when the traumatic injury benefit is paid.

facts.name: Rider Termination Age
facts.sentence: The rider terminates at the insured's age 55.

facts.name: Rider Termination Timing
facts.sentence: The rider terminates upon occupational separation, whichever occurs later.

facts.name: Family Readiness Benefit
facts.sentence: Rider 2 is called the Family Readiness Benefit Rider.

facts.name: Annual Premium for Family Readiness Rider
facts.sentence: The annual premium for Rider 2 is $80 per year.

facts.name: Family Support During Deployment
facts.sentence: Rider 2 is designed to assist military families during deployment.

facts.name: Family Support Stipend
facts.sentence: If the insured is deployed to a Declared Combat Zone, the rider pays a monthly family support stipend of $300 per month.

facts.name: Max Family Support Duration
facts.sentence: The maximum duration of the monthly family support stipend under Rider 2 is 36 months over the policy life.

facts.name: Family Stipend Start Timing
facts.sentence: The family support stipend under Rider 2 begins 60 days after confirmed deployment orders.

facts.name: No Elimination Period for First Deployment
facts.sentence: There is no elimination period for the first deployment after the policy date under Rider 2.

facts.name: Family Support Stipend Funding Source
facts.sentence: Funding for the family support stipend under Rider 2 comes from the rider premium.

facts.name: Family Stipend Non-Diminishing
facts.sentence: The family support stipend under Rider 2 does not reduce the death benefit.

facts.name: Family Support Stipend Initiation
facts.sentence: To initiate the family support stipend under Rider 2, the insured must submit a DD-214 or deployment orders.

facts.name: Waiver of Premium – Combat Disability
facts.sentence: Rider 3 is called the Waiver of Premium – Combat Disability Rider.

facts.name: Waiver of Premium Cost
facts.sentence: The annual premium for Rider 3 is $75 per year.

facts.name: Waiver of Premium: Combat Disability
facts.sentence: If the insured is 100% disabled due to a combat-related injury, as determined by the VA or a DoD Physical Evaluation Board, all premiums are waived.

facts.name: Waiver of Premium Continues Full Coverage
facts.sentence: When premiums are waived under Rider 3, coverage continues in full.

facts.name: Lifelong Premium Waiver
facts.sentence: The waiver of premiums under Rider 3 continues for life or until death, whichever comes first.

facts.name: Lifelong Premium Waiver
facts.sentence: Rider 3 does not terminate at age 65.

facts.name: Lifelong Premium Waiver
facts.sentence: Rider 3 lasts for life.

facts.name: VA 100% Disability Trigger
facts.sentence: A VA rating of 100% disability from any service-connected condition triggers the waiver under Rider 3.

facts.name: Waiver Trigger Scope
facts.sentence: The trigger for the waiver under Rider 3 is not limited to combat-related injuries.

facts.name: Occupational Separation Notification
facts.sentence: Upon occupational separation from military service, the insured must notify Valor Life within 90 days.

facts.name: Post-Separation Surcharge Removal
facts.sentence: After occupational separation, military and combat surcharges are removed.

facts.name: Premium Recalculation Post-Separation
facts.sentence: Following occupational separation, the premium is recalculated at civilian rates based on attained age.

facts.name: Occupational Separation Continuity
facts.sentence: No evidence of insurability is required after occupational separation.

facts.name: Coverage Retention Post-Separation
facts.sentence: The coverage amount remains unchanged after occupational separation.

facts.name: Surcharges Removed Upon Reinstatement
facts.sentence: Surcharges are removed.

facts.name: Premium Recalculation by Age
facts.sentence: The premium is recalculated at civilian rates based on attained age.

facts.name: No Evidence Required
facts.sentence: No evidence of insurability is required.

facts.name: Coverage Amount Stability
facts.sentence: The coverage amount remains unchanged.

facts.name: Reinstatement After Re-enlistment
facts.sentence: If the insured re-enlists or enters reserve duty after separation, they may request reinstatement of military coverage terms.

facts.name: Reinstatement with War Coverage
facts.sentence: Reinstatement of military coverage terms includes full war coverage.

facts.name: Reinstatement Requires Written Notification
facts.sentence: Request for reinstatement requires written notification.

facts.name: Reinstatement Requires Proof
facts.sentence: Request for reinstatement requires proof of service.

facts.name: No Re-Underwriting for Reinstatement
facts.sentence: Re-underwriting is not required for reinstatement.

facts.name: Surcharges Based on Duty Status
facts.sentence: Surcharges are reapplied based on new duty status.

facts.name: Officer Status Surcharge Review
facts.sentence: Transition to officer status does not automatically change the surcharge class.

facts.name: Occupational Review Upon Officer Transition
facts.sentence: A new occupational review is conducted when transitioning to officer status.

facts.name: Annual Premium Amount
facts.sentence: Total annual premium is $1,291.00.

facts.name: Premium Due Date
facts.sentence: Due date for total annual premium is February 19 each year.

facts.name: Monthly Payment Through Military Pay System
facts.sentence: Monthly payment mode is available through the military pay system.

facts.name: Monthly Allotment Availability
facts.sentence: Payment via monthly allotment is available through MyPay/DFAS.

facts.name: Monthly Payment Amount
facts.sentence: Monthly payment amount is $112.40.

facts.name: No Fee for Monthly Allotments
facts.sentence: There is no service fee for monthly allotment payments.

facts.name: Deployment Grace Period Extension
facts.sentence: If the insured is deployed and cannot make payment during the standard 31-day grace period, the grace period is automatically extended.

facts.name: Deployment Grace Period Extension
facts.sentence: Deployment-related grace period extension is up to 90 days.

facts.name: Grace Period Extension via Deployment Orders
facts.sentence: Extension of grace period requires submission of deployment orders.

facts.name: Deployment Grace Extension Access
facts.sentence: The insured or a designated Power of Attorney can invoke the deployment grace period extension.

facts.name: Deployment Grace Period Invocation
facts.sentence: Invocation of the deployment grace period extension can occur via written notice.

facts.name: Deployment Grace Period Invocation
facts.sentence: Invocation of the deployment grace period extension can occur via electronic notice.

facts.name: Deployment Lapse Reinstatement
facts.sentence: Any policy lapsed due to deployment within 2 years may be reinstated.

facts.name: Deployment Reinstatement Without Evidence
facts.sentence: Reinstatement of a lapsed policy due to deployment does not require evidence of insurability.

facts.name: Reinstatement Requires Back Premiums
facts.sentence: Back premiums must be paid for reinstatement.

facts.name: Reinstatement Interest Charge
facts.sentence: An additional 5% interest applies to back premiums for reinstatement.

facts.name: Conversion Privilege Access
facts.sentence: The insured may convert to a permanent policy at any time.

facts.name: Conversion Right Before 20th Anniversary
facts.sentence: The insured may convert to a permanent policy at any time before the policy's 20th anniversary.

facts.name: Conversion Before Age 58
facts.sentence: The insured may convert to a permanent policy at any time before age 58.

facts.name: Conversion Deadline Rule
facts.sentence: The earlier of the policy's 20th anniversary or age 58 determines the latest allowable conversion time under Section 5.1.

facts.name: Conversion Without Evidence
facts.sentence: No evidence of insurability is required when converting to a permanent policy under Section 5.1.

facts.name: One-Time Conversion Option
facts.sentence: Upon occupational separation from active duty service, the insured has a one-time conversion option.

facts.name: Conversion Window After Separation
facts.sentence: The one-time conversion option upon occupational separation is exercisable within 365 days of separation.

facts.name: Conversion Option Post-Separation
facts.sentence: There are no age restrictions on the conversion option available upon occupational separation.

facts.name: Conversion After Separation
facts.sentence: There are no anniversary restrictions on the conversion option available upon occupational separation.

facts.name: Conversion Override for Separation
facts.sentence: Section 5.2 overrides any age or anniversary restrictions otherwise applicable under Section 5.1 for conversions triggered by occupational separation.

facts.name: Incontestability Clause
facts.sentence: After two years from the policy date, this policy shall not be contested during the insured's lifetime.

facts.name: Non-Payment Exception
facts.sentence: The only exception to the non-contestability clause is non-payment of premiums.

facts.name: Policy Incontestability After Two Years
facts.sentence: The policy becomes uncontested after two years from the policy date, provided the insured is still alive.

facts.name: Post-two-year contestability exception
facts.sentence: Non-payment of premiums remains a valid basis for contesting the policy even after two years.

facts.name: Governing Law Clause
facts.sentence: This policy is governed by the laws of the State of Virginia.

facts.name: Domicile of Valor Life
facts.sentence: Valor Life is domiciled in the State of Virginia.

facts.name: Policy Issuance Location
facts.sentence: The policy was issued in Arlington, Virginia.

facts.name: CEO Signature on Policy
facts.sentence: The Chief Executive Officer of Valor Life Insurance Company signed the policy.

facts.name: Signature Title Verification
facts.sentence: The signature block includes the title 'Chief Executive Officer'.

facts.name: Policy Issuance Date
facts.sentence: The date of issuance is February 19, 2024.

facts.name: Basic Life Coverage Amount
facts.sentence: Basic Life coverage amount is $150,000.

facts.name: Guaranteed Issue for Basic Life
facts.sentence: Basic Life coverage is guaranteed issue and does not require Evidence of Insurability (EOI).

facts.name: Guaranteed Issue Supplemental Life
facts.sentence: Supplemental Life coverage up to $300,000 is available through guaranteed issue.

facts.name: Supplemental Life Enrollment Window
facts.sentence: Supplemental Life coverage can be elected only during the initial enrollment window.

facts.name: Initial Enrollment Window Duration
facts.sentence: The initial enrollment window for Supplemental Life coverage lasts 31 days from the date of hire.

facts.name: EOI Requirement for Late Enrollment
facts.sentence: Evidence of Insurability (EOI) is required for Supplemental Life coverage if enrollment occurs after the initial enrollment window.

facts.name: EOI Requirement for Increased Coverage
facts.sentence: Evidence of Insurability (EOI) is required for Supplemental Life coverage if coverage increases occur outside of open enrollment periods.

facts.name: EOI Requirement for Excess Coverage
facts.sentence: Evidence of Insurability (EOI) is required for Supplemental Life coverage if the total coverage exceeds $300,000.

facts.name: Spouse Dependent Life Amount
facts.sentence: Spouse Dependent Life coverage amount is $50,000.

facts.name: Spouse Coverage Guarantee
facts.sentence: Spouse Dependent Life coverage is guaranteed issue when enrolled within the initial enrollment window.

facts.name: Children Coverage Guarantee
facts.sentence: Children Dependent Life coverage is always guaranteed issue regardless of enrollment timing.

facts.name: Active Work Requirement
facts.sentence: Life insurance coverage becomes effective only on days when the employee is actively working.

facts.name: Coverage Effective Date Rule
facts.sentence: If an employee is not actively working on the effective date of coverage, coverage begins on the first day they return to active work.

facts.name: Death Benefit Payment Process
facts.sentence: Upon submission of satisfactory proof of death, both the basic and supplemental life benefits will be paid to the designated beneficiary.

facts.name: Death Benefit Payment Timeline
facts.sentence: The death benefit payment for basic and supplemental life policies will be made within 30 days of receiving satisfactory proof of death.

facts.name: Suicide Exclusion Waiver After 12 Months
facts.sentence: No suicide exclusion applies under the group life plan after the employee’s first 12 months of participation.

facts.name: Suicide Refund Policy
facts.sentence: During the first 12 months of participation, death due to suicide triggers a refund of premiums paid by the employee.

facts.name: Employer Premium Forfeiture
facts.sentence: Premiums paid by the employer for the basic life component are not refunded upon death by suicide during the first 12 months; these premiums are forfeited to the plan.

facts.name: Suicide Premium Refund Clause
facts.sentence: Death by suicide within the first 12 months results in a return of premiums paid by the employee.

facts.name: Suicide Death Premium Forfeiture
facts.sentence: Premiums paid by the employer for the basic plan are forfeited to the plan if death by suicide occurs within the first 12 months.

facts.name: Seat Belt Bonus Benefit
facts.sentence: If death occurs in an automobile accident and the insured was wearing a seat belt at the time of death, an additional 10% of the life benefit is paid.

facts.name: Seat Belt Benefit Maximum
facts.sentence: The maximum amount payable under the seat belt benefit is $25,000.

facts.name: Felony Murder Exclusion
facts.sentence: No death benefit is payable to a beneficiary who feloniously and intentionally causes the death of the insured.

facts.name: Felony Exclusion Payout Rule
facts.sentence: In cases where the beneficiary caused the death feloniously and intentionally, the death benefit is paid to the contingent beneficiary.

facts.name: Beneficiary Felony Exclusion
facts.sentence: In cases where the beneficiary caused the death feloniously and intentionally, the death benefit is paid to the employee's estate.

facts.name: ADB Coverage Eligibility
facts.sentence: Accelerated Death Benefit (ADB) is available on both the basic and supplemental life coverage combined.

facts.name: Accelerated Death Benefit Eligibility
facts.sentence: An individual qualifies for ADB if they are diagnosed with a terminal illness and have a life expectancy of twelve months or less.

facts.name: Accelerated Death Benefit Advance
facts.sentence: Up to 80% of the total life benefit may be advanced through the Accelerated Death Benefit.

facts.name: Accelerated Death Benefit Cap
facts.sentence: The maximum amount that can be advanced via the Accelerated Death Benefit is $360,000.

facts.name: No Actuarial Discount for ADB
facts.sentence: There is no actuarial discount applied when advancing the Accelerated Death Benefit.

facts.name: Accelerated Death Benefit Lump Sum
facts.sentence: The Accelerated Death Benefit is paid in a single lump sum payment.

facts.name: Remaining Life Benefit Payout
facts.sentence: The remaining portion of the life benefit is paid to the beneficiary upon the insured’s death.

facts.name: Accelerated Benefit & Dependent Coverage
facts.sentence: Dependent coverage is unaffected by the receipt of the Accelerated Death Benefit.

facts.name: EAP Bereavement Access
facts.sentence: All certificate holders have access to Pinnacle's Employee Assistance Program (EAP) Bereavement Services upon a covered death.

facts.name: Family Access to EAP Bereavement Services
facts.sentence: Immediate family members of certificate holders have access to Pinnacle's Employee Assistance Program (EAP) Bereavement Services upon a covered death.

facts.name: Grief Counseling Access
facts.sentence: Pinnacle's EAP Bereavement Services include up to five sessions of grief counseling.

facts.name: Grief Counseling Delivery Options
facts.sentence: Grief counseling provided through Pinnacle's EAP Bereavement Services may be conducted in person or via telehealth.

facts.name: EAP Claim Concierge Service
facts.sentence: Claim assistance concierge service is included in Pinnacle's EAP Bereavement Services.

facts.name: EAP Bereavement Resources
facts.sentence: Estate administration resource referrals are included in Pinnacle's EAP Bereavement Services.

facts.name: Free EAP Bereavement Access
facts.sentence: Access to Pinnacle's EAP Bereavement Services incurs no cost to the user.

facts.name: EAP Bereavement Services Included
facts.sentence: Pinnacle's EAP Bereavement Services are included as part of the group plan.

facts.name: Employee Coverage Portability
facts.sentence: The employee may port supplemental life coverage upon termination of employment.

facts.name: Portability Eligibility Condition
facts.sentence: Termination of employment must occur for a reason other than non-payment of premiums to qualify for portability.

facts.name: Coverage Continuation via Portability
facts.sentence: Ported coverage allows continuation of the supplemental life coverage at group rates.

facts.name: Portability Without Medical Proof
facts.sentence: No evidence of insurability is required to port coverage.

facts.name: Portability Coverage Limit
facts.sentence: The ported coverage can continue up to the full face amount in force at termination.

facts.name: Ported Coverage Duration
facts.sentence: Ported coverage continues as individual group-rate coverage for five years.

facts.name: Port Coverage Age Limit
facts.sentence: Ported coverage continues until age 70, whichever occurs first.

facts.name: Portability Election Deadline
facts.sentence: An election to port coverage must be made within 31 days of termination.

facts.name: Direct Billing of Ported Coverage
facts.sentence: Premiums for ported coverage will be direct-billed.

facts.name: Conversion to Permanent Policy
facts.sentence: The employee may convert any or all group life coverage to an individual permanent life insurance policy.

facts.name: Conversion Policy Issuer
facts.sentence: The individual permanent life insurance policy is issued by Pinnacle Individual Life.

facts.name: Affiliate Relationship
facts.sentence: Pinnacle Individual Life is an affiliate of Pinnacle Group Benefits.

facts.name: No Evidence of Insurability Required
facts.sentence: Conversion to an individual policy does not require evidence of insurability.

facts.name: Conversion Deadline
facts.sentence: A conversion election must be made within 31 days of losing group coverage.

facts.name: Conversion Premium Basis
facts.sentence: Premiums on the converted policy are based on attained age.

facts.name: Conversion Premium Basis
facts.sentence: Premiums on the converted policy are based on standard underwriting class.

facts.name: Conversion Rate Limitations
facts.sentence: Preferred rates are not guaranteed on the converted policy.

facts.name: Dependent Coverage Eligibility
facts.sentence: Dependent life coverage includes coverage for a spouse or child.

facts.name: Dependent Eligibility Loss via Divorce
facts.sentence: A dependent may lose eligibility due to divorce.

facts.name: Dependent Eligibility Loss
facts.sentence: A dependent may lose eligibility when a child reaches the plan’s maximum age.

facts.name: Dependent Coverage Conversion
facts.sentence: Dependent life coverage may be converted to individual coverage.

facts.name: Dependent Coverage Conversion Window
facts.sentence: The conversion of dependent coverage must occur within 31 days of losing eligibility.

facts.name: Marriage as Qualifying Event
facts.sentence: Marriage qualifies as a qualifying life event for enrollment changes.

facts.name: Divorce as Qualifying Event
facts.sentence: Divorce qualifies as a qualifying life event for enrollment changes.

facts.name: Child Birth Event Eligibility
facts.sentence: Birth of a child qualifies as a qualifying life event for enrollment changes.

facts.name: Adoption as Qualifying Event
facts.sentence: Adoption of a child qualifies as a qualifying life event for enrollment changes.

facts.name: Spouse’s Coverage Loss Event
facts.sentence: Loss of another group coverage by a spouse qualifies as a qualifying life event.

facts.name: Qualifying Life Event Enrollment
facts.sentence: Enrollment changes triggered by a qualifying life event allow enrollment or increased coverage outside of annual open enrollment.

facts.name: Life Event Enrollment Deadline
facts.sentence: Changes related to a qualifying life event must be elected within 31 days of the event.

facts.name: Annual Open Enrollment Timing
facts.sentence: Annual open enrollment occurs each year, typically in November.

facts.name: Annual Coverage Increase
facts.sentence: During annual open enrollment, employees may increase supplemental coverage.

facts.name: Annual Coverage Increase Limit
facts.sentence: Employees may increase supplemental coverage by up to one salary multiple during annual open enrollment.

facts.name: 31-Day Qualifying Event Window
facts.sentence: There are 31 days of the qualifying event.

facts.name: Annual Coverage Increase Without EOI
facts.sentence: Each year, typically in November, employees may increase supplemental coverage by up to one salary multiple without evidence of insurability.

facts.name: Annual Open Enrollment Increase
facts.sentence: An employee can increase supplemental coverage from two times their salary to three times their salary during Annual Open Enrollment.

facts.name: Annual Enrollment Coverage Limit
facts.sentence: During Annual Open Enrollment, increases in supplemental coverage are limited to the plan maximum of $500,000 total supplemental coverage.

facts.name: FMLA Leave Coverage Continuity
facts.sentence: Coverage continues in full during approved Family Medical Leave Act (FMLA) leave for up to 12 weeks.

facts.name: Premium Payments During FMLA Leave
facts.sentence: Employees must continue making premium payments during approved FMLA leave.

facts.name: FMLA Premium Payment Arrangement
facts.sentence: Employers are responsible for establishing a payment arrangement for premiums during the FMLA leave period.

facts.name: Employer Plan Amendment Rights
facts.sentence: The employer Northridge Medical Systems, Inc. may amend the group plan with 60 days’ notice to covered employees.

facts.name: Employer Plan Suspension Rights
facts.sentence: The employer Northridge Medical Systems, Inc. may suspend the group plan with 60 days’ notice to covered employees.

facts.name: Employer Plan Termination Notice
facts.sentence: The employer Northridge Medical Systems, Inc. may terminate the group plan with 60 days’ notice to covered employees.

facts.name: Insurer Non-Renewal Right
facts.sentence: The insurer may choose not to renew the group policy on its annual renewal date with 90 days’ notice to the employer.

facts.name: Conversion Rights After Termination
facts.sentence: Upon plan termination, all covered employees are entitled to exercise conversion rights as described in Section 3.2.

facts.name: Maximum Combined Coverage Limit
facts.sentence: The maximum combined coverage amount for basic and supplemental life insurance is $2,000,000 per individual.

facts.name: Excess Coverage Underwriting Requirement
facts.sentence: Any coverage exceeding $2,000,000 requires separate underwriting.

facts.sentence: The group policy is governed by the laws of the State of Ohio.

facts.name: Definition of Active Tranche
facts.sentence: An 'Active Tranche' is defined as any coverage tranche that has not yet reached its scheduled expiration date.

facts.name: Total Death Benefit Definition
facts.sentence: The 'Total Death Benefit' is defined as the sum of all active tranche face amounts at the time of the insured's death.

facts.name: Tranche Conversion Definition
facts.sentence: ‘Tranche Conversion’ is defined as the exercise of the right to convert an individual tranche to a permanent policy.

facts.name: Death Benefit Payout Condition
facts.sentence: We will pay the Total Death Benefit to the beneficiary upon the insured's death while this policy is in force.

facts.name: Premiums Current for Payout
facts.sentence: Payment of the Total Death Benefit occurs when all premiums are current.

facts.name: Timely Death Benefit Payout
facts.sentence: The Total Death Benefit is payable within 30 days of satisfactory proof of death.

facts.name: Suicide Exclusion Clause
facts.sentence: Death by suicide within 2 years of policy issuance is excluded from coverage.

facts.name: Death During Policy In Force
facts.sentence: This policy provides coverage for the insured's death while the policy is in force.

facts.name: Premium Currentness Requirement
facts.sentence: All premiums under this policy must be current for coverage to remain effective.

facts.name: Death Benefit Payout Timeline
facts.sentence: Payment of the death benefit occurs within 30 days of receiving satisfactory proof of death.

facts.name: Suicide Exclusion Within Two Years
facts.sentence: Death by suicide within two years of the policy date results in a benefit limited to the return of premiums paid without interest.

facts.name: Suicide Exclusion Lifted After Two Years
facts.sentence: After two years from the policy date, full total death benefit is payable even in cases of suicide.

facts.name: Aviation Exclusion by Tranche
facts.sentence: A standard aviation exclusion applies only to Tranche 3.

facts.name: Aviation Coverage for Tranches 1 & 2
facts.sentence: Tranches 1 and 2 provide full coverage regardless of aviation activity, including operation of private aircraft.

facts.name: Aviation Exclusion Based on Pilot Status
facts.sentence: The differential aviation exclusion structure exists due to the insured’s declared recreational pilot status.

facts.name: Aviation Exclusion & Premium Discount
facts.sentence: The differential aviation exclusion structure accounts for the correspondingly lower premium for Tranche 3.

facts.name: Single Claim for Multiple Tranches
facts.sentence: A single claim and proof of death apply to all active tranches.

facts.name: Combined Disbursement Policy
facts.sentence: Payment for all active tranches is made in one combined disbursement.

facts.name: Waiver Premium Amount
facts.sentence: The Waiver of All Tranche Premiums – Disability rider has an annual premium of $155.
chunk_topics: Waiver of All Tranche Premiums – Disability

facts.name: Total Disability Definition
facts.sentence: Total disability is defined as being unable to engage in any gainful occupation for which the insured is suited by education, training, or experience.

facts.name: Disability Duration Requirement
facts.sentence: The disability condition must last for six or more consecutive months prior to age 60 to trigger the waiver.

facts.name: Waived Premiums During Disability
facts.sentence: During the disability period, all tranche premiums are waived.

facts.name: Full Coverage During Disability
facts.sentence: Coverage in all active tranches continues in full during the disability period.

facts.name: Waiver Duration Conditions
facts.sentence: The waiver remains in effect until the insured recovers, returns to work, or reaches age 65.

facts.name: Premiums Resume on Recovery
facts.sentence: Upon recovery, regular premiums resume for the insured.

facts.name: Waiver of Rider Premium During Disability
facts.sentence: The premium for the waiver of premium rider is also waived during the disability period.

facts.name: Waiver Eligibility Based on Tranche 3 Expiry
facts.sentence: If disability begins before the expiration of Tranche 3 (in 2034), the waiver covers premiums of all tranches that are currently active.

facts.name: Accelerated Death Benefit Access
facts.sentence: An accelerated death benefit is available with no additional premium cost.

facts.name: Accelerated Death Benefit Eligibility
facts.sentence: Acceleration is permitted upon diagnosis of a terminal illness with a life expectancy of twelve months or less.

facts.name: Accelerated Death Benefit Limit
facts.sentence: Up to 75% of the total death benefit at the time of acceleration may be accessed.

facts.name: Accelerated Death Benefit Cap
facts.sentence: The maximum amount accessible through the accelerated death benefit is $1,500,000.

facts.name: Accelerated Benefit Priority
facts.sentence: The accelerated death benefit is drawn first from Tranche 1.

facts.name: Terminal Illness Qualification
facts.sentence: Terminal illness qualifies for accelerated death benefits if life expectancy is less than or equal to 12 months.

facts.name: Terminal Illness Acceleration
facts.sentence: Up to 75% of the total death benefit is available upon acceleration due to terminal illness.

facts.name: Terminal Illness Payout Cap
facts.sentence: The maximum amount payable under terminal illness acceleration is $1,500,000.

facts.name: Tranche 1 First Payment Priority
facts.sentence: Benefit payments during terminal illness are drawn from Tranche 1 first.

facts.name: Tranche Payment Sequence
facts.sentence: After Tranche 1 is exhausted, benefit payments proceed to Tranche 2.

facts.name: Actuarial Discount Rate
facts.sentence: An actuarial discount of approximately 7% per year applies based on remaining life expectancy.

facts.name: Tranche 3 Exemption Condition
facts.sentence: Terminal illness acceleration does not impact Tranche 3 unless specifically requested.

facts.name: Independent Tranched Conversion
facts.sentence: Each tranche can be converted independently to a permanent life insurance policy.

facts.name: No Evidence of Insurability Required
facts.sentence: Conversion of a tranche does not require evidence of insurability.

facts.name: Tranche Conversion Termination
facts.sentence: Converting a tranche terminates that tranche under the current policy.

facts.name: Tranche Conversion Continuity
facts.sentence: Remaining tranches continue unaffected after a tranche conversion.

facts.name: Tranche Conversion Deadline
facts.sentence: A tranche must be converted before its expiration date or the insured’s 70th birthday, whichever comes first.

facts.name: Minimum Conversion Amount
facts.sentence: The minimum face amount eligible for conversion is $100,000.

facts.name: Tranche Face Amount Reduction
facts.sentence: The insured may reduce the face amount of any tranche on any policy anniversary.

facts.name: Written Reduction Request Requirement
facts.sentence: Reduction requests must be made in writing.

facts.name: Irrevocable Tranche Reduction
facts.sentence: A reduction in a tranche’s face amount is irrevocable.

facts.name: Premium Adjustment After Reduction
facts.sentence: Premiums are adjusted downward when a tranche’s face amount is reduced.

facts.name: Minimum Tranche Face Amount After Reduction
facts.sentence: The minimum remaining face amount for any tranche after reduction is $100,000.

facts.name: Tranche Cancellation Independence
facts.sentence: Any individual tranche may be cancelled without affecting other tranches.

facts.name: Irreversible Tranche Cancellation
facts.sentence: Cancellation of a tranche is irrevocable.

facts.name: Irreversible Tranche Cancellation
facts.sentence: Once cancelled, a tranche cannot be reinstated.

facts.name: Tranche Lapse Priority Rule
facts.sentence: If premiums remain unpaid beyond the grace period, coverage lapses on the tranche with the shortest remaining coverage period first.

facts.name: Sequential Lapse Prioritization
facts.sentence: Lapse occurs sequentially across tranches, prioritizing those with shorter durations.

facts.name: Lapse Prevention Priority
facts.sentence: This sequence preserves longer-duration tranches whenever possible.

facts.name: Sequential Lapse Protection
facts.sentence: The purpose of the sequential lapse provision is to protect the insured’s long-term coverage during financial hardship.

facts.name: Tranche Addition Restriction
facts.sentence: No new tranches may be added to the policy after the policy date.

facts.name: Tranche Addition Limitation
facts.sentence: Additional term coverage requires a new policy.

facts.name: Long-Term Coverage Protection
facts.sentence: The policy provides protection for the insured's long-term coverage in cases of financial hardship.

facts.name: No Post-Issuance Tranche Additions
facts.sentence: No new tranches may be added to this policy after the policy date.

facts.name: New Coverage Requires New Application
facts.sentence: Additional term coverage requires a new policy application.

facts.name: Total Annual Premium Amount
facts.sentence: The total annual premium amount is $2,790.00.

facts.name: Premium Due Date
facts.sentence: The due date for the total annual premium is June 1 each year.

facts.name: Annual Premium Payment
facts.sentence: The payment mode for the premium is annual.

facts.name: Quarterly Payment Option
facts.sentence: A quarterly payment option is available at $722.85 per quarter.

facts.name: Premium Allocation to Tranche 1
facts.sentence: Premiums are allocated among tranches as follows: Tranche 1 receives $1,890.00.

facts.name: Tranche 2 Premium Allocation
facts.sentence: Premiums are allocated among tranches as follows: Tranche 2 receives $620.00.

facts.name: Tranche 3 Premium Allocation
facts.sentence: Premiums are allocated among tranches as follows: Tranche 3 receives $280.00.

facts.name: Rider Fee Amount
facts.sentence: Riders are charged $155.00 in total.

facts.name: Rider Allocation Rule
facts.sentence: Rider charges are allocated proportionally to Tranche 1.

facts.name: Grace Period Duration
facts.sentence: The grace period for premium payments is 31 days from the due date.

facts.name: Policy Reinstatement Window
facts.sentence: Reinstatement of the policy is allowed within 2 years of lapse.

facts.name: Reinstatement Requirement
facts.sentence: To reinstate the policy, all back premiums must be paid.

facts.name: Reinstatement Interest Requirement
facts.sentence: An additional 7% interest must be paid when reinstating the policy.

facts.name: Reinstatement Requirement
facts.sentence: Evidence of insurability must be provided to reinstate the policy.

facts.name: Reinstatement Limitation
facts.sentence: Reinstatement does not restore any tranche that was previously cancelled.

facts.name: Reinstatement Scope Limitation
facts.sentence: Reinstatement only applies to lapsed tranches.

facts.name: Contestability Period Start
facts.sentence: The contestability period begins on the policy date.

facts.name: Contestability Period Duration
facts.sentence: The contestability period lasts for 2 years from the policy date.

facts.name: Contestability Period End
facts.sentence: Contestability ends after 2 years from the policy date during the insured's lifetime.

facts.name: Post-Two-Year Incontestability
facts.sentence: After 2 years from the policy date, the insurer will not contest the policy unless there is non-payment of premiums.

facts.name: Tranche-Specific Contestability
facts.sentence: Each tranche has its own contestability period.

facts.name: Tranche Contestability Start Date
facts.sentence: The contestability period for each tranche runs from the policy date.

facts.name: Contestability Period Timing
facts.sentence: The contestability period for each tranche does not run from the tranche's expiration date.

facts.name: Ability Period Start Date
facts.sentence: The ability period runs from the policy date.

facts.name: Ability Period Timing
facts.sentence: The ability period does not run from the tranche's expiration date.

facts.name: Governing Law Jurisdiction
facts.sentence: This policy is governed by the laws of the State of Minnesota.

facts.name: Policy Issuance Location
facts.sentence: The policy was issued in Minneapolis, Minnesota.

facts.name: Policy Signed by President
facts.sentence: The President and Chief Actuary of Cornerstone Life & Annuity Insurance Company signed the policy.

facts.name: Policy Identification Number
facts.sentence: The policy number is TP-STD-2024-2288.

facts.name: Policy Effective Date
facts.sentence: The policy date is September 9, 2024.

facts.name: Survivorship Policy Type
facts.sentence: The policy type is 20-Year Survivorship Level Term (Second-to-Die).

facts.name: First Insured: Robert Pemberton
facts.sentence: The first insured is Robert Allen Pemberton.

facts.name: Male Insured Identification
facts.sentence: Robert Allen Pemberton is male.

facts.name: Birth Date of Robert Pemberton
facts.sentence: Robert Allen Pemberton was born on March 12, 1955.

facts.name: Issue Age: 69
facts.sentence: Robert Allen Pemberton’s issue age is 69.

facts.name: Underwriting Classification: Table C
facts.sentence: Robert Allen Pemberton’s underwriting class is Standard Non-Smoker – Rated Table C.

facts.name: Prostate Cancer in Remission
facts.sentence: Robert Allen Pemberton has a medical history that includes prostate cancer diagnosed in 2019 and currently in remission.

facts.name: Mild Coronary Artery Disease
facts.sentence: Robert Allen Pemberton has mild coronary artery disease that is stable and medicated.

facts.name: Second Insured Identified
facts.sentence: The second insured is Margaret Louise Pemberton.

facts.name: Gender of Second Insured
facts.sentence: Margaret Louise Pemberton is female.

facts.name: Birthdate of Margaret Pemberton
facts.sentence: Margaret Louise Pemberton was born on July 3, 1957.

facts.name: Issue Age: Margaret Pemberton
facts.sentence: Margaret Louise Pemberton’s issue age is 66.

facts.name: Preferred Underwriting Status
facts.sentence: Margaret Louise Pemberton’s underwriting class is Preferred Non-Smoker.

facts.name: Osteoporosis Management
facts.sentence: Margaret Louise Pemberton has osteoporosis that is managed.

facts.name: No Cardiovascular History
facts.sentence: Margaret Louise Pemberton has no cardiovascular history.

facts.name: Survivorship Policy Structure
facts.sentence: This policy is a survivorship life insurance policy.

facts.name: Death Benefit Trigger Condition
facts.sentence: This policy pays the death benefit only upon the death of the second insured to die.

facts.name: No Benefit on First Death
facts.sentence: No death benefit is paid upon the death of the first insured.

facts.name: Survivorship Coverage Continuation
facts.sentence: Coverage remains in force following the death of the first insured.

facts.name: Post-First Death Premium Payments
facts.sentence: Premium payments continue after the death of the first insured.

facts.name: Continued Premiums Until Second Death
facts.sentence: Premium payments continue until the second insured dies or the policy expires.

facts.name: Underwriting Advantage in Survivorship Policy
facts.sentence: Robert Pemberton’s underwriting rating (Table C) has a substantially lower impact on this survivorship policy’s premium compared to its impact on an individual policy.

facts.name: Reduced Impact of Table C Rating
facts.sentence: The reason for reduced impact of Robert Pemberton’s Table C rating is that the benefit is not paid until both insureds have died.

facts.name: Trust Establishment Date
facts.sentence: The Pemberton Dynasty Trust established on August 1, 2024.

facts.name: Trustee Appointment
facts.sentence: William James Pemberton serves as the trustee of The Pemberton Dynasty Trust.

facts.name: Trust Tax ID Number
facts.sentence: The taxpayer identification number of The Pemberton Dynasty Trust is 92-7734119.

facts.name: Trust Beneficiary Designation
facts.sentence: The beneficiary of The Pemberton Dynasty Trust is the issue of Robert and Margaret Pemberton, per stirpes.

facts.name: Base Policy Face Amount
facts.sentence: The face amount of the base policy is $1,500,000.

facts.name: Policy Duration and Expiration
facts.sentence: The policy period of the base policy lasts 20 years and expires on September 9, 2044.

facts.name: Base Policy Annual Premium
facts.sentence: The annual premium for the base policy is $19,440.00.

facts.name: Total Annual Premium with Riders
facts.sentence: The total annual premium for the base policy including riders is $20,620.00.

facts.name: Lower Premium Impact of Table C
facts.sentence: Table C has a substantially lower impact on this survivorship policy's premium compared to its impact on an individual policy.

facts.name: Benefit Payout Timing
facts.sentence: The benefit under this survivorship policy is not paid until both insureds have died.

facts.name: Definition of Second Insured to Die
facts.sentence: The term 'Second Insured to Die' refers to the surviving insured at the time of the later death of the two insureds.

facts.name: Joint Life Expectancy Definition
facts.sentence: The term 'Joint Life Expectancy' refers to the actuarially estimated period until the death of the second surviving insured.

facts.name: Survivor Paid-Up Provision Definition
facts.sentence: The Survivor Paid-Up Provision refers to the feature described in Section 1.3.

facts.name: Second Insured Death Coverage
facts.sentence: The policy provides coverage for the death of the second insured to die during the 20-year policy period.

facts.name: Named Beneficiary
facts.sentence: The named beneficiary of the policy is the Pemberton Dynasty Trust.

facts.name: Second Death Benefit Payout
facts.sentence: The policy pays $1,500,000 to the Pemberton Dynasty Trust upon satisfactory proof of the death of the second insured to die during the 20-year policy period.

facts.name: First Death Benefit Exclusion
facts.sentence: No benefit is paid upon the death of the first insured to die.

facts.name: Policy Continuity After First Death
facts.sentence: The policy remains in force following the death of the first insured to die.

facts.name: Survivor Premium Waiver Option
facts.sentence: If Robert Allen Pemberton dies first, Margaret Louise Pemberton may elect, within 90 days of Robert's death, to stop paying premiums.

facts.name: Survivor Paid-Up Option
facts.sentence: If Margaret Louise Pemberton elects to stop paying premiums after Robert Allen Pemberton’s death, she accepts a paid-up reduced death benefit.

facts.name: Reduced Paid-Up Benefit Calculation
facts.sentence: The reduced paid-up benefit is calculated actuarially based on the reserve at the time of election relative to the premiums otherwise due.

facts.name: Irrevocable Election Clause
facts.sentence: Any election under the Survivor Paid-Up Provision is irrevocable.

facts.name: Continuing Premium Option
facts.sentence: Alternatively, Margaret Louise Pemberton may choose to continue paying premiums after Robert Allen Pemberton’s death.

facts.name: Maintain Full Death Benefit
facts.sentence: If Margaret Louise Pemberton continues paying premiums, she maintains the full $1,500,000 death benefit.

facts.name: Survivor Premium Choice
facts.sentence: The decision between stopping premium payments or continuing them is solely up to Margaret Louise Pemberton.

facts.name: Written Illustration Within 30 Days
facts.sentence: The insurance company will provide a written illustration of both the reduced-paid-up option and the continued-full-benefit option within 30 days of the first death.

facts.name: Suicide Exclusion Clause
facts.sentence: If either insured dies by suicide within 2 years of the policy date, the policy remains in force for the surviving insured's benefit.

facts.name: Suicide Exclusion Impact
facts.sentence: If either insured dies by suicide within 2 years of the policy date, the death benefit payable upon the second insured's death is reduced by the amount of premiums paid after the suicide of the first insured.

facts.name: Suicide Death Premium Return
facts.sentence: If both insureds die by suicide within 2 years of the policy date, only the premiums paid are returned.

facts.name: Simultaneous Death Payout Rule
facts.sentence: If both insureds die in the same event and it cannot be determined who died first, the benefit is paid as if Margaret Louise Pemberton survived Robert Allen Pemberton.

facts.name: Contractual Order of Survival
facts.sentence: The policy includes a contractual order of survival.

facts.name: Assumed Survival Order
facts.sentence: If the deaths of Robert Allen Pemberton and Margaret Louise Pemberton occurred simultaneously, it is assumed that Margaret Louise Pemberton survived Robert Allen Pemberton.

facts.name: Survival Assumption Rule
facts.sentence: The assumption that Margaret Louise Pemberton survived Robert Allen Pemberton applies when it cannot be determined who lived longer.

facts.name: Order of Survival Rule
facts.sentence: The benefit under the policy is paid as though Margaret Louise Pemberton survived Robert Allen Pemberton.

facts.name: Contractual Order of Survival
facts.sentence: This order of survival is specified in the contract.

facts.name: Felonious Death Exclusion
facts.sentence: No benefit is payable if the death of the surviving insured is caused feloniously by a beneficiary of the trust.

facts.name: Trust Reform Upon Felony Death
facts.sentence: If the death of the surviving insured is caused feloniously by a beneficiary of the trust, the trust distribution must be reformed.

facts.name: Beneficiary Exclusion Due to Felony
facts.sentence: When the death of the surviving insured is caused feloniously by a beneficiary of the trust, the beneficiary must be excluded from the trust distribution.

facts.name: Beneficiary Felony Exclusion
facts.sentence: When the death of the surviving insured is caused feloniously by a beneficiary of the trust, the benefit is paid to the trust.

facts.name: Beneficiary Felony Exclusion
facts.sentence: When the death of the surviving insured is caused feloniously by a beneficiary of the trust, the trust distributes the benefit to the remaining trust beneficiaries.

facts.name: No War Exclusion
facts.sentence: This policy contains no war exclusion.

facts.name: No War Exclusion Coverage
facts.sentence: Death resulting from any cause, including acts of war, is covered under this policy.

facts.name: First Death Notification Benefit
facts.sentence: Rider 1 provides a First Death Notification Benefit.

facts.name: Rider 1 Premium
facts.sentence: The premium for Rider 1 is $480 per year.

facts.name: First Death Benefit
facts.sentence: A lump-sum payment of $50,000 is made upon the death of the first insured to die.

facts.name: First-Death Benefit Recipient
facts.sentence: The recipient of the $50,000 payment under Rider 1 is the policy owner, which is the trust.

facts.name: First-Death Estate Support
facts.sentence: The purpose of the $50,000 payment under Rider 1 is to assist with estate settlement costs.

facts.name: First-Death Funeral Assistance
facts.sentence: The purpose of the $50,000 payment under Rider 1 is to assist with funeral costs.

facts.name: First-Death Transition Support
facts.sentence: The purpose of the $50,000 payment under Rider 1 is to assist with transition costs associated with the first death.

facts.name: First-Death Benefit Non-Reduction
facts.sentence: The $50,000 payment under Rider 1 does not reduce the $1,500,000 survivorship death benefit.

facts.name: First Death Proof Requirement
facts.sentence: Payment under Rider 1 requires proof of the first death.

facts.name: First Death Proof Deadline
facts.sentence: Proof of the first death must be submitted within 21 days.

facts.name: First Death Benefit Exclusivity
facts.sentence: Rider 1 is the only benefit payable upon the first death.

facts.name: Rider 1 Termination Condition
facts.sentence: Rider 1 terminates once the first-death payment is made.

facts.name: Accelerated Benefit – Terminal Illness
facts.sentence: Rider 2 provides an Accelerated Benefit for Terminal Illness for the surviving insured.

facts.name: Rider 2 Premium
facts.sentence: The premium for Rider 2 is $380 per year.

facts.name: Post-First Death Benefit Activation
facts.sentence: Rider 2 applies after the death of the first insured.

facts.name: Accelerated Benefit Eligibility
facts.sentence: An accelerated benefit under Rider 2 can be accessed if the surviving insured is diagnosed with a terminal illness.

facts.name: Terminal Illness Qualification
facts.sentence: A diagnosis qualifies for the accelerated benefit under Rider 2 if life expectancy is less than or equal to 12 months.

facts.name: Accelerated Benefit Limit
facts.sentence: Up to 70% of the remaining death benefit may be advanced under Rider 2.

facts.name: Accelerated Benefit Discount
facts.sentence: Advancement of benefits under Rider 2 is subject to an 8% per annum actuarial discount.

facts.name: Trusted Authorization Requirement
facts.sentence: Trustee authorization is required before an advance is made under Rider 2.

facts.name: Survivor Benefit Payout
facts.sentence: The remaining portion of the death benefit under Rider 2 is paid to the trust upon the death of the surviving insured.

facts.name: Early Death Benefit Advance
facts.sentence: Up to 70% of the remaining death benefit may be advanced.

facts.name: Death Benefit Advance Discount
facts.sentence: The advance on the death benefit is subject to an 8% per annum actuarial discount.

facts.name: Death Benefit Advance Authorization
facts.sentence: Trustee authorization is required before any advance on the death benefit can be made.

facts.name: Trust Payout After Second Death
facts.sentence: The remaining death benefit will be paid to the trust upon the death of the surviving insured.

facts.name: Premium Continuation First Death Waiver
facts.sentence: Rider 3 is called 'PREMIUM CONTINUATION – FIRST DEATH WAIVER'.

facts.name: Annual Premium for Rider 3
facts.sentence: The annual premium for Rider 3 is $320.

facts.name: First Death Premium Waiver
facts.sentence: If Robert dies first, all remaining premiums under the policy are waived.

facts.name: Full Coverage Post-First Death
facts.sentence: Coverage under the policy continues at the full amount of $1,500,000 after the first insured’s death.

facts.name: Continued Coverage After First Death
facts.sentence: Coverage continues until the second insured dies or the policy expires.

facts.name: Premium Waiver After First Death
facts.sentence: This rider ensures that the surviving spouse or trust is not burdened with ongoing premiums after the first death.

facts.name: First Death Waiver Coverage
facts.sentence: This rider applies regardless of which insured dies first.

facts.name: Change of Insured Provision
facts.sentence: Section 3 outlines the Change of Insured Provision.

facts.name: Spouse Substitution After Remarriage
facts.sentence: If either insured remarries after the death of the other insured, the owner (trustee) may request substitution of the new spouse as the surviving insured.

facts.name: Age Requirement for Spouse Substitution
facts.sentence: The new spouse must be between the ages of 45 and 80.

facts.name: New Spouse Underwriting Requirement
facts.sentence: The new spouse must submit to full underwriting.

facts.name: Premium Adjustment After Underwriting
facts.sentence: A premium adjustment reflecting the new underwriting class is required.

facts.name: Change-of-Insured Timing Limit
facts.sentence: This change-of-insured provision is available only in Year 1 following the first insured's death.

facts.name: Change of Insured Eligibility Condition
facts.sentence: This change-of-insured provision is only available if Premium Continuation Rider (Rider 3) has not yet been triggered.

facts.name: Total Annual Premium
facts.sentence: The total annual premium for the main policy is $20,620.00.

facts.name: Annual Premium Due Date
facts.sentence: The due date for the total annual premium is September 9 each year.

facts.name: Annual Payment Mode
facts.sentence: The payment mode for the total annual premium is annual.

facts.name: Annual Premium Payment Method
facts.sentence: The total annual premium is paid from the trust checking account via ACH.

facts.name: Grace Period Duration
facts.sentence: There is a grace period of 62 days from the due date for premium payments.

facts.name: Extended Grace Period Benefit
facts.sentence: The extended grace period allows additional time for premium payment.

facts.name: Annual Premium Due Date
facts.sentence: The annual due date for the policy premium is September 9.

facts.name: Annual Premium Payment
facts.sentence: The payment mode for the policy premium is annual.

facts.name: ACH Payment Method
facts.sentence: The payment method for the policy premium is via ACH from the trust checking account.

facts.name: Grace Period Duration
facts.sentence: The grace period for the policy premium is 62 days from the due date.

facts.name: Extended Grace Period Purpose
facts.sentence: The extended grace period allows additional time for trust administration to arrange payment.

facts.name: Premium Waiver Upon First Death
facts.sentence: If Rider 3 (Premium Continuation) is triggered following the first death, no further premiums are due.

facts.name: Rider 3 Triggers Premium Waiver
facts.sentence: If Rider 3 (Premium Continuation) is triggered following the first death, Section 4.3 becomes moot.

facts.name: Premium Waiver Confirmation Timeline
facts.sentence: Within 30 days of the first insured’s death, the company will issue a written confirmation of premium waiver to the trustee.

facts.name: Policy Conversion Right
facts.sentence: The owner may convert the survivorship term policy to a survivorship permanent policy without evidence of insurability.

facts.name: Conversion to Permanent Policies
facts.sentence: The type of survivorship permanent policy available for conversion includes whole life or universal life.

facts.name: Conversion Deadline Window
facts.sentence: The deadline for converting the survivorship term policy to a survivorship permanent policy is before the earlier of the policy's 15th anniversary or the younger insured's 80th birthday.

facts.name: Survivor Conversion Right
facts.sentence: After the death of the first insured, the surviving insured may convert the remaining coverage to an individual permanent life policy.

facts.name: Survivor Conversion Right
facts.sentence: The surviving insured may convert the remaining coverage to an individual permanent life policy without evidence of insurability.

facts.name: Conversion Window Post-First Death
facts.sentence: The timeframe for the surviving insured to exercise the conversion right is within 1 year of the first insured's death.

facts.name: Conversion Limit Post-Death
facts.sentence: The conversion amount for the surviving insured cannot exceed the original face amount of the policy.

facts.name: Policy Incontestability Timeline
facts.sentence: This policy becomes incontestable after 2 years from the policy date.

facts.name: Joint Lifetime Incontestability
facts.sentence: The policy becomes incontestable only when both insureds are alive jointly.

facts.name: Incontestability Exception
facts.sentence: The incontestability provision does not apply to non-payment of premiums.

facts.name: Post-Death Contestability Period
facts.sentence: After the first insured's death, a separate 2-year contestability period begins for the surviving insured.

facts.name: Survivor Contestability Period
facts.sentence: The second 2-year contestability period applies specifically to the surviving insured's participation in the application.

facts.name: Governing Law Jurisdiction
facts.sentence: This policy is governed by the laws of the State of Florida.

facts.name: Policy Issuance Location
facts.sentence: The policy was issued in Tampa, Florida.
